1	# Metrics — the lessons' indicators as git commands
2	
3	L3 292: "Git log will give this directly." Every indicator below is one command against this repo.
4	`CHAIN` is a chain directory, e.g. `intent/0004-lesson-only`. `created` (first conversation) is the
5	one value git does not know; the capture-intent skill puts it on the PR body's first line, read with
6	`gh pr view <n> --json body`.
7	
8	## L2 capture-intent (233–239)
9	- Leading — time from first conversation to committed intent.md: the PR body's first line versus
10	  `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%aI %h' -- $CHAIN/intent.md`
11	- Lagging — survival rate (accepted = merged, closed = rejected):
12	  `gh pr list --state all --search 'intent.md' --json number,state,title`
13	- Lagging — intent.md changed after the first spec.md commit:
14	  `git log --format=%h --since="$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%aI -1 -- $CHAIN/spec.md)" -- $CHAIN/intent.md`
15	
16	## L3 requirements-and-design (288–294)
17	- Leading — intent.md commit → spec.md commit (two timestamps):
18	  `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%aI %f' -- $CHAIN/intent.md $CHAIN/spec.md`
19	- Lagging — spec.md commits dated after the first plan.md commit:
20	  `git log --format=%h --since="$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%aI -1 -- $CHAIN/plan.md)" -- $CHAIN/spec.md`
21	
22	## L4 plan-mode (362–366)
23	- Leading — share of planned PR slices merged from the first implementation pass: use
24	  `gh pr list --state all --search "$CHAIN" --json number,state,title` to locate the PRs, then read
25	  their review/rework evidence. Multiple planned PRs in one chain are not rework; PR count or CLOSED
26	  state alone does not establish a first-pass result.
27	- Leading — the recorded human acceptance time of the applicable plan revision → that slice's PR merge.
28	  Read the document/SHA and decision record per GIT-WORKFLOW; stage acceptance need not be a document merge.
29	  `gh pr list --state merged --json number,title,mergedAt --search "$CHAIN"` supplies merge times only.
30	- Lagging — does the merged diff still match plan.md's "Files that change":
31	  `gh pr diff <n> --name-only` for the PR that carried the code, then read the list against the
32	  applicable plan revision's current PR slice by eye; future slices are not missing from this PR.
33	  (Not `<plan commit>..HEAD` — that picks up every later chain's files; measured on 0008.)
34	- Lagging — rework cycles per change: `gh pr view <n> --json reviews,commits --jq '{reviews: (.reviews|length), commits: (.commits|length)}'`
35	
36	## L5 CLAUDE.md (442)
37	- Leading — corrections/changes to CLAUDE.md: `git log --oneline -- CLAUDE.md`
38	- Lagging — outside this repo (new-joiner time-to-first-merged-PR is org PR history)
39	
40	## L6 skills (505)
41	- Leading — policy-owner sign-off → skill merge: `git log --diff-filter=AM --format='%aI %h' -- .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
42	- Lagging — outside this repo (review findings citing the policy are read by a person on the PR)
43	
44	## L7 hooks-as-build-time-guardrails (511)
45	No separate "How to measure it" section — it rides on L6's (505); nothing to add here.
46	
47	## L8 parallel sessions and subagents (588)
48	- Leading — outside this repo (concurrent sessions per engineer is the OTel export)
49	- Lagging — merges per week: `git log --since=1.week --oneline --merges | wc -l | tr -d ' '` (rework rate is outside this repo)
50	
51	## L9 feedback loop (659)
52	- Leading — first-pass CI success: `gh run list --workflow=check.yml --json conclusion,event`
53	- Lagging — review time: `gh pr view <n> --json createdAt,mergedAt`
54	  (change failure rate is outside this repo, from an incident tracker)
55	
56	## L10 continuous evals (729)
57	- Leading — pass rate over time: each `agent evals` run uploads `evals/out` as the artifact
58	  `evals-<run id>` (`gh run download <run id>`); a person reads the series of `*.json` (no script here)
59	- Leading — incident → permanent eval, for an incident born in this repo's monitoring (`ops/bands.yaml`):
60	  `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%cI %h' -- intent/<NNNN>-*/intent.md evals/cases/<NN>-*.json`
61	  (chain 0006: 3 min 39 s). Incidents tracked outside the repo start from the tracker's timestamp.
62	- Lagging — outside this repo (regressions caught in CI vs found in production is an incident tracker)
63	
64	## L11 AI in the PR review loop (795)
65	- Leading — time to first review: `gh pr view <n> --json createdAt,reviews,comments --jq '[.reviews[].submittedAt, .comments[].createdAt] | min'`
66	  (this repo's findings arrived as comments, so `reviews` alone is null)
67	- Leading — review comments resolved without a human touching the branch: `gh pr view <n> --json comments,commits`
68	  — count comments answered by a commit whose author is the agent's session, not a person; a person reads it
69	- Lagging — outside this repo (pre/post-merge defects need an incident tracker)
70	
71	## L12 hooks as approval gates (930)
72	- Leading — gate wait time and verdict: `.claude/hooks.log` (the decision log this repo writes), summed by a person
73	- Lagging — outside this repo (gate violations reaching production is an incident tracker)
74	
75	## L13 CI/CD integration and deployment (997)
76	- Leading — share of pipeline failures triaged without paging a human: failed `check` runs
77	  (`gh run list --workflow=check.yml --json databaseId,conclusion`) that carry a `triage-<run id>`
78	  artifact (`gh run view <id>`), over all failed runs. The triage step only runs with the key.
79	- Lagging — outside this repo (DORA measures come from CI/deploy tooling itself)
80	
81	## L14 closing the loop on metrics (1063)
82	- Leading — band breach → intent.md in the triage queue: the breach time is the `detected_at` the
83	  detector wrote into the draft's `Author:` line; the queue time is that file's first commit —
84	  `grep -h '^Author: detect_bands' intent/*/intent.md` against
85	  `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%cI %h' -- intent/*/intent.md` (chain 0006: 16 s)
86	- Lagging — outside this repo (repeat-incident rate is an incident tracker)
87	
88	Nothing here is computed by a script. The numbers are for a person to read once a quarter.
